tasks.title: Replace PTY output integer arrays with generation-14 base64
tasks.objective: Deliver the smallest end-to-end protocol and SDK change that carries PTY output as canonical padded base64 while preserving raw-byte replay, validation, queue accounting, and public client behavior.
tasks.outcome: Rust daemon and TypeScript SDK agree on generation 14: JSON output chunks are strict padded standard-base64, SDK callers receive decoded Uint8Array bytes, malformed or non-canonical payloads fail closed, and frozen reliability budgets remain unchanged.
acceptance: The protocol generation advances to 14 and OutputChunk retains raw Vec<u8> internally while its only JSON representation is canonical padded standard base64; old integer-array and dual-encoding fallbacks are removed.
Rust wire-shape tests prove exact encoding, round-trip decoding, and rejection of invalid, unpadded, non-canonical, whitespace-containing, and non-zero trailing-bit base64.

The SDK decodes output bytes once to Uint8Array, rejects malformed base64 and range/decoded-length mismatches at the owning paths, and does not perform per-byte validation calls; input payload encoding remains unchanged.
Attachment event budgeting and replay helpers count decoded raw bytes, with a bounded two-chunk test proving one-megabyte raw accounting differs from base64 character accounting.
The frozen reliability-budgets.json numbers and frozen_before_optimization marker are unchanged, and reliability qualification passes from a clean committed source tree.

Generated protocol declarations, public documentation, CLI/SDK smoke paths, full unit/integration tests, formatting, static checks, and local-consumer checks agree on generation 14 and the decoded-byte API.

Four temporary implementation mutations are exercised and reverted: integer-array serialization, missing range-length validation, illegal-character acceptance, and encoded-character queue accounting; each owning assertion turns red without leaving a mutation behind.

verification.proves: Rust formatting is clean for the protocol and client changes.
Repository TypeScript and Markdown formatting is clean.
Generation-14 wire encoding, strict decoding, and protocol fuzz tests pass with non-zero executed counts.
SDK unit, malformed-input, parser-fuzz, and public Rust/TypeScript end-to-end tests pass.
